1) simulating historical low nitrogen-winter dry conditions in a Colorado mixed-grass prarie resulted in a plant commmunity dominated by historically abundant grassland species, 2) the same plant community was observed in the first year of an extreme precipitation event, and 3) native grasses and forb productivity were unaffected by either of these treatments.

1) the plant community composition in this mixed-grass meadows is shifting from a native-dominated community to a community with a high abundance of introduced species, 2) this change is driven by a reduction in atmospheric N and winter precipitation, and 3) the plant community is highly responsive to an extreme winter precipitation event, but not to a reduction in atmospheric nitrogen.
